question.prompt: The traffic on a certain east-west highway moves at a constant speed of \(60\) miles per hour in both directions. An eastbound driver passes \(20\) westbound vehicles in a five-minute interval. Assume vehicles in the westbound lane are equally spaced. Which of the following is closest to the number of westbound vehicles present in a \(100\)-mile section of highway?

solutions.explanation:
Because the vehicles approach one another, their speeds add. The westbound traffic moves past the driver at \(60+60=120\) miles per hour. Five minutes is \(1/12\) hour, so the driver encounters a stretch of westbound traffic of length
\[
120\cdot\frac1{12}=10\text{ miles}.
\]
Twenty vehicles in about \(10\) miles suggests \(2\) vehicles per mile, or about \(200\) in \(100\) miles.

The interval endpoints do not make this estimate exact, but we can check that they cannot change the choice. Let \(s>0\) be the spacing in miles. The \(20\) encountered vehicles span \(19\) complete gaps. The observation interval extends at most one spacing before the first vehicle and after the last, so
\[
19s\le10\le21s.
\]
Consequently \(190\le100/s\le210\). If \(N\) vehicles occupy a \(100\)-mile section, the same gap reasoning gives
\[
(N-1)s\le100\le(N+1)s,
\]
so \(189\le N\le211\). Every count in this range is closest to \(\boxed{200}\) among the offered values. The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
solutions.title: Use relative speed to estimate the spacing
